title: Super Weights Are Critical to Read — But Useless to Train Alone
hook: A handful of parameters wreck accuracy if removed. You'd think training just those would be the cheapest fine-tune ever. It isn't — it collapses the model to random guessing instead.
key_points: 'Super Weights' are individual parameters whose removal degrades model performance by orders of magnitude — but this paper shows the effect doesn't hold universally across all LLMs.
Training only the Super Weight parameters in isolation (100 to 8,192 of them) drops OLMo-1B and OLMo-7B accuracy to random-guessing levels.
Expanding to local neighborhoods around Super Weights (up to 36K parameters) still gives no improvement.

Training an equal number of randomly chosen positions in the same down_proj layers instead improves over baseline — so the failure is specific to targeting Super Weight coordinates, not to sparsity itself.
Vanilla LoRA succeeds using only 0.16% of parameters, updating every position in attention weights (and down_proj) through a low-rank structure instead of hand-picking coordinates.
content_html: If a handful of parameters are so important that deleting them wrecks a model, training just those parameters should be the ultimate cheap fine-tune. This paper shows that logic backfires completely.
extra_html: "Super Weights" are individual parameters whose removal is known to degrade model performance by orders of magnitude — though the authors first note this effect doesn't hold universally across every LLM. The real test is training: isolating and training only the Super Weight parameters (ranging from 100 up to 8,192 of them) drops both OLMo-1B and OLMo-7B to random-guessing accuracy. Widening the net to local neighborhoods around those weights, up to 36K parameters, doesn't help either. The tell is a control experiment: training an equal number of randomly chosen positions in the same down_proj layers actually improves over baseline — so the collapse traces specifically to targeting Super Weight coordinates, not to training a small parameter subset in general. Meanwhile, vanilla LoRA succeeds with just 0.16% of parameters, because it updates every position in the attention weight matrices (and down_proj) through a structured low-rank decomposition rather than cherry-picking individually "important" coordinates — a result the authors confirm holds up across a 10-seed ablation. The lesson: a parameter being important doesn't mean it's trainable in isolation; effective fine-tuning needs structured updates across whole layers. From arXiv, 2026-07-09.

related.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation
related.hook: Why retrain billions of weights when you can freeze them all and train tiny add-on matrices instead? LoRA tunes under ~1% of the parameters with near-full-fine-tune quality.

related.title: QLoRA: Fine-tuning Quantized LLMs
related.hook: Fine-tune a model with tens of billions of parameters on a single GPU. QLoRA squeezes the frozen base to 4-bit, then trains LoRA adapters on top — without losing quality.

related.title: Toy Models of Superposition
related.hook: Why is a single neuron so hard to interpret? It may be doing several jobs at once. Networks pack more features than they have neurons by overlapping them.

flashcards.prompt: What's counterintuitive about training Super Weights in isolation?
flashcards.back_html: Super Weights are critical enough that removing them tanks performance by orders of magnitude, yet training only those parameters (even up to 8,192 of them) collapses OLMo-1B/7B accuracy to random guessing rather than helping.

flashcards.prompt: What shows the collapse is specific to targeting Super Weight coordinates, not just training too few parameters?

choices.text: Training an equal number of randomly chosen positions in the same down_proj layers improves over baseline instead of collapsing
Training more Super Weight neighbors always fixes the collapse
The collapse also happens when training full layers

flashcards.explanation_html: Same parameter count, same layers, different coordinates: random positions in down_proj help, while Super Weight coordinates collapse the model — pointing at the specific coordinates, not sparsity, as the cause.

flashcards.prompt: Why does vanilla LoRA succeed where directly training Super Weights fails?
flashcards.back_html: LoRA updates every position in attention weight matrices (and down_proj) through a structured low-rank decomposition, using only 0.16% of parameters — rather than hand-picking a small set of individually 'important' coordinates.
